title: Sarma (Rice-Stuffed Vine Leaves with Lemon and Herbs)
summary: Rice cooked with onion, tomato paste, lemon and currants, mixed with pine nuts and herbs, rolled in vine leaves and simmered gently under a plate in lemony water and olive oil. Served at room temperature.
equipment: wide heavy saucepan (about 24 cm) with lid
small heatproof plate that fits inside the pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: 44 for rolling and about 11 to line the pan; rinsed well

ingredients.item: lemon, cut into wedges, to serve

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Warm the 80 ml oil in the sauté pan over medium heat and cook the onion with the salt and pepper for 8-10 min until soft and just catching. Stir in the tomato paste for 2 min until the oil turns red. Add the rice, 240 ml water, 60 ml lemon juice and the currants and simmer gently for 12-15 min, stirring now and then, until the liquid is absorbed but the rice is still firm in the centre. Off the heat, stir in the pine nuts, parsley and mint and leave to cool.

steps.title: Prepare the leaves
steps.text: Separate the vine leaves in the warm water, rinse twice and drain. Pick out 44 whole leaves and snip off any stems. Line the base of the saucepan with the torn or spare leaves.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Lay a leaf vein side up with the stem end towards you. Put a level tablespoon of filling near the stem, shape it into a 5 cm log, fold in the sides and roll up firmly but not tightly. Pack the rolls seam side down in tight rows in the pan, making a second layer if needed.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour over the 300 ml water, 60 ml lemon juice and 40 ml oil, cover with any leftover leaves and press down with the plate. Cover, bring to a simmer and cook on low for 40-45 min until the rice is tender. Cool in the pan, then serve at room temperature or cold with lemon wedges.

tips: Rolling too tightly makes the rolls burst as the rice swells.
Fresh vine leaves work too: blanch them in boiling water for 1 minute first.
They taste even better the next day.
storage: Refrigerate in their cooking liquid up to 4 days. Serve at room temperature. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
